Chapter 6: The Road to Change—Examinations and the Dream of Escape.
There comes a point in every young person’s life when everything seems to narrow down to just one thing—a big test, a single decision, or one moment that feels like it could change everything.
For this boy, that moment is the national college entrance exam. Around the village, folks talk about these exams in hushed tones—part awe, part anxiety. For most, it’s a far-off hope, almost impossible to reach. But at the same time, it’s a doorway—a chance to step beyond the fields and escape the heavy pull of family history.
The months leading up to these exams are filled with a quiet, almost electric intensity. Night after night, the boy studies under the soft glow of his lamp, long after everyone else has gone to bed. His mother slips quietly into his room, bringing a bowl of rice or a couple of boiled eggs, her face caught between pride and worry. His father can’t help with the lessons, but he sits close by, offering his silent support. The air in their home grows thick with anticipation, with hope, and with all the fears that no one dares to speak aloud.
Meanwhile, outside, life in the village goes on—fields to work, animals to tend, neighbors to greet. But for the boy, everything else fades away. The pressure is enormous. He knows all the sacrifices his family has made, their dreams for something better, rest entirely on his shoulders. Sometimes, the weight feels too much. There are moments when he worries he just can’t carry it.
He thinks about a neighbor’s son—a few years older—who dreamed of leaving the village too, but didn’t pass the exams. Now, that boy works in the fields, his dreams quietly tucked away. That memory is both a warning and a push. The boy tells himself, “That can’t be me.”
When exam day finally arrives, he walks to the testing center with nerves twisting in his stomach. The room is packed with hopeful faces, each carrying their own stories and their own dreams. The questions are tough, and the hours seem to stretch on forever. He feels the eyes of the proctors, the weight of expectation, and the silent prayers of his family echoing in his mind.
And then, at last, the results arrive. The village holds its breath. The boy’s family gathers around as he opens the letter, his hands shaking. It’s good news—better than anyone dared hope. He’s passed. Relief washes over the family, mixed with joy and a hint of disbelief. Suddenly, the future feels wide open. The mountains that once felt like walls now look a little more like gateways.
But even in this moment of triumph, there’s a bittersweet ache. Leaving the village means letting go of everything familiar—his family, his friends, all the routines he’s ever known. The excitement of what’s possible is blended with the pain of saying goodbye. He sees it in his parents’ eyes: so much pride, but also a quiet sadness. They’ve given him wings, but now he has to use them to fly away.
The journey to the city, to university, is both thrilling and a little scary. The boy steps onto the bus with just a small bag and a heart full of hope—and fear. The road winds through mountains, past fields and villages, carrying him toward a world he’s only ever read about in stories. As the scenery shifts and the city draws near, something changes inside him too. The boy who once felt trapped by his past now dares to imagine a different kind of future—one he just might be able to create for himself.
